name: Fern & Kettle
description: A made-up two-person online tea shop (loose-leaf tea, a few teapots), used as the example team. Nothing here is a real business.

humans.name: Ana
humans.summary: Owner. Talks to Ops; decisions and approvals only.

humans.name: Leo
humans.summary: Partner. Same as Ana: either one can approve.

roles.name: Ops
roles.summary: Orchestrator: the owners' only contact. Routes every request, decides by the authority levels whether an owner is needed, tracks promises, closes each request with a receipt

roles.name: Retro
roles.summary: Weekly retro: audits how the team worked (receipts, promises, approvals, cost) and proposes up to 3 changes by PR

roles.name: Dev
roles.summary: The storefront code: pages, checkout, fixes; picks up the backlog

roles.name: Reviewer
roles.summary: Reviews every pull request once (the merge gate merges what it passes)

roles.name: Marketing
roles.summary: Product pages, newsletter drafts, what to promote this week

roles.name: Support
roles.summary: Customer questions, order problems, reply drafts

rules: Level 2 of the authority levels below, unless a standing decision (precedent) covers it.
Emails always go through propose_email: an owner's own "approve" sends them.
Changing production outside a reviewed pull request.

levels.heard: the log and the office's Done today
examples: a reply draft within the support policy
a PR that changes a page's copy or layout
money: ads, a new paid tool, a supplier order
prices, discounts and refunds beyond the support policy
anything sent to customers outside the templates
a leaked key or odd access

rules: The teammate proposes the level and Ops checks it; when they differ, the higher one wins.
In doubt between two levels, the higher one, once: the owner's answer becomes a precedent (remember, precedent: true).
An owner's request approves what was asked, and only that. What a PR does beyond it follows the levels.
Trust ladder: after 10 approvals in a row without changes, Ops proposes moving that category down a level (an owner approves). One incident moves it back up at once.

heartbeat.prompt: Backlog ({now}): {why}. Pick up what's yours or chase whoever has it (one clear task each). Don't merge: the gate does. If nothing needs action, post_update one line and stop.

routines.name: morning-check
routines.prompt: Morning check ({now}): run the tests on a clean checkout, list PRs open for more than a day. If something is wrong, fix it by PR or share it (urgent only if checkout is affected).

routines.name: weekly-promo
routines.prompt: Weekly promo ({now}): pick one product to feature this week and draft the newsletter. Ask for approval with the draft; nothing goes out without it.

triggers.name: new-support-tickets
triggers.prompt:
New customer messages ({name}). Draft a reply for each and send the drafts to the owners in one request_approval:
{items}
